facts.topic: CubeStore symbols/dates: types and order
facts.detail: CubeStore.symbols is a plain List[str] (store.meta['symbols'], or synthesized 's{i}' if absent); CubeStore.dates is a List[str] of YYYYMMDD strings. Both come straight from dt_meta.json with no transformation. date_range() casts dates to int and uses np.searchsorted, so dates must already be ascending; SegmentedCubeStore enforces self.dates == sorted(self.dates) at construction.
facts.refs: store.py:104-105 (CubeStore.__init__); store.py:195-202 (date_range); store.py:303-304 (SegmentedCubeStore ascending-date assertion)

facts.topic: CubeStore.view() symbol order is NOT re-sorted
facts.detail: view(symbols=[...]) builds sym_idx by looking up each requested symbol in a fresh {symbol:index} dict and keeps the CALLER's order (no sort). Only when symbols=None does it fall back to np.arange (store's own order). max_symbols just truncates after that.
facts.refs: store.py:204-219 (CubeStore.view)

facts.topic: SegmentedCubeStore.symbols is base-order-then-appended, not globally sorted
facts.detail: self.symbols = base_symbols + extra, where base_symbols is the base store's own saved order and extra is sorted(union of later segments' symbols - base_symbols) appended AFTER all base symbols regardless of numeric value. Confirmed in practice: base store has 5207 symbols (minute/dt_meta.json), but the live SegmentedCubeStore Partura's build_shared.py opened on 2026-10-04 reported 5220 symbols (view.symbols printed in shared/README.txt) -- 13 symbols added by the 6 incremental segments, appended at the tail, not interleaved by ticker. Any new side-store MUST align by symbol STRING, never by positional index copied from one store object into another.
facts.refs: store.py:305-307 (SegmentedCubeStore.__init__); server:/root/autodl-tmp/qmt_daily_data/fast_factor_compute/minute/dt_meta.json (n_symbols=5207); /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/shared/README.txt on server ("x 5220 symbols"); /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/build_shared.py:43

facts.topic: warmed_view: what it does and does not change
facts.detail: warmed_view(store, start, end, warmup, symbols, max_symbols) first builds base = store.view(...) for the requested [start,end] window, then sets d0 = max(0, base.d0 - warmup) and returns CubeView(store, base.sym_idx, d0, base.d1) plus trim = base.d0 - d0. It only ever moves the day-axis start earlier, in trading-day row units (not calendar days); it never touches symbols/sym_idx. trim can be SMALLER than the requested warmup when the store has insufficient history before start (left-censoring) -- callers must slice [trim:] after evaluation, which is exactly what evaluate_factors does.
facts.refs: research.py:82-86 (warmed_view); research.py:110-111 (warm budget = max_window(...,'D') + warmup_buffer); research.py:117-120,132 (trim applied post-evaluation)

facts.topic: CubeView row-chunk/day-chunk reading and the subset-view row mapping
facts.detail: CubeView.sym_idx (int64 ndarray) is the row number into the underlying STORE's own arrays, not a 0..n index; view.symbols/view.dates are plain string lists built once in __init__ ([store.symbols[i] for i in sym_idx], store.dates[d0:d1]) and are never cached as dicts anywhere in store.py. read_s(name,s_lo,s_hi) and read_d(name,d_lo,d_hi) address the VIEW's own local 0-based symbol/day axis; _rows() converts a contiguous run of sym_idx to a slice (cheap stripe read) or else falls back to fancy indexing.
facts.refs: store.py:406-447 (CubeView, _rows, read_s, read_d, tradable)

facts.topic: tearsheet.index_members and list_day: ListDays is already synthesized purely from the cube, with left-censoring
facts.detail: index_members() takes list_day (a per-symbol row index, NOT a calendar date) and compares (t - list_day) >= min_age. list_day itself is built in tradable_backtest.py's prepare step as np.argmax(alive, axis=1) over the VIEW's own day_status!=OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE plane, with list_day forced to -10_000 for any symbol already alive on the view's first day (i.e. 'listed before this window, exact date unknown to the cube'). This is exactly the left-censoring problem a security_master-based ListDays field would fix.

facts.topic: daily_capital/<date>.parquet columns and verified share-count semantics
facts.detail: Columns: date, symbol, day_status, circulating_capital, total_capital, circulating_market_value, total_market_value. Verified numerically on 20230807.parquet (4927 rows): circulating_market_value/circulating_capital and total_market_value/total_capital produce IDENTICAL describe() statistics (mean 22.32, min 1.29, max 1887.93 CNY/share) -- i.e. both 'capital' columns ARE share counts (not monetary capital) sharing one implied per-share price; circulating_capital <= total_capital holds for all 4926 TRADING rows. units block in daily_capital/_meta.json confirms: {'capital':'share','market_value':'CNY'}. Symbol format is 'NNNNNN.SZ'/'NNNNNN.SH', byte-identical to the cube's own symbol format (minute/dt_meta.json symbols sample) and to security_master.parquet's symbol column.

facts.topic: daily_capital causality evidence: share-count fields are quarter-end-anchored, not trade-date-anchored; price timing not independently verified
facts.detail: quality/<date>.parquet (18 cols incl. field, status, raw_value, used_value, source_effective_date, candidate_effective_date, raw_effective_date, observed_at, availability, date_quality) shows, for trade_date=20230807, source_effective_date=candidate_effective_date=raw_effective_date='20230630' (prior quarter end) for ordinary SOURCE_ACCEPTED_UNVERIFIED rows; source_effective_date==trade_date for only 0.47% of that date's 9854 quality rows (mostly REVIEWED_OVERRIDE cases, e.g. 688347.SH where raw_value is NaN and used_value is a manually-anchored override). This means the SHARE-COUNT denominator legitimately lags to the last disclosed filing (not a look-ahead issue, since quarterly filings are public well before the next quarter's trading days), but it also means a naive 'same trade_date' assumption is wrong for ~99.5% of rows. observed_at timestamps (2026-09-15/09-17) show the whole 2018-2026 history was BATCH-CONSTRUCTED/backfilled in Sept 2026, not fed live day-by-day. Status counts for 20230807: SOURCE_ACCEPTED_UNVERIFIED 9824, MATERIAL_CHANGE_UNVERIFIED 28, REVIEWED_OVERRIDE 2 (only 2 of 9854 rows actually had raw_value != used_value on this sample date). The PRICE side of market_value's own timing (day-t close vs day-(t-1) close) was deliberately NOT verified against the cube's Close field in this phase (would require reading a cube .npy, outside the parquet/json-only mandate for this recon pass) -- flagged as an open question.

result.summary: Read-only store-data recon for the AlphaCube daily-field side-store, covering both the local code (store.py, research.py, tradability.py, label.py, tearsheet.py, Partura's build_shared.py/bridge.py/guard.py) and read-only server inspection (daily_capital, fast_factor_compute, qmt_stock_data/processed, Partura's server shared/). Headline findings: (1) CubeStore/CubeView symbols and dates are always plain Python str lists with NO cached symbol/date->index dict anywhere, and critically, SegmentedCubeStore.symbols is base-order-then-appended-extras (NOT globally sorted) -- so any new sidecar must align strictly by symbol/date STRING, never by position copied from a live view (verified concretely: base store has 5207 symbols, the live segmented store Partura last opened had 5220). warmed_view only shifts the day-axis start earlier in trading-day units and reports a trim count; symbols are untouched. (2) On the server, daily_capital/<date>.parquet (2114 files, 20180102..20260916, symbol format identical to the cube's) is exactly tearsheet.load_caps's existing source for circulating/total market value and share counts (verified numerically), but it sits beside an unused-by-current-code point-in-time bookkeeping system (first_used/, quality/, versions/) whose quality/ schema proves share-count values are anchored to quarter-end disclosure dates, not trade_date -- a real but nuanced causality subtlety current consumers (tearsheet.py, build_shared.py) don't account for; the PRICE-side day-t-vs-day-(t-1) timing was deliberately left unverified since confirming it would require a non-parquet/json (.npy) read outside this pass's mandate. (3) Of the requested fields, FloatCap/TotalCap/FloatShares/TotalShares/ListDays genuinely need the new sidecar (security_master.parquet gives a non-left-censored list_date and a CURRENT-ONLY ST proxy via name prefix), while Board and LimitWidth need no new data file at all -- tradability.board_limit already derives both purely from symbol-string prefixes. (4) The cube's own incremental segments and daily_capital's batch ingestion are independently paced (concretely: one symbol, 301655.SZ, is in daily_capital's latest file but in no cube segment yet), so the sidecar needs its own explicit append/rebuild step; nothing in store.py keeps it current automatically. Facts below carry file:line or exact server-path/query refs; insertion_points flag where a daily_fields.py-style module, the engine/parser hookup (outside this file set), the build script, and the causality check itself should land; open_questions lists what was deliberately left unverified rather than guessed.
